**I'm coming back to say that this game is incredibly addictive and actually really fun and strategic once you've played it for about 15 hours. There are a ton of glitches and sometimes the game will just stop working altogether in the middle of an hour-long level, but when you learn how to work around most of the glitches, it's pretty fun. My biggest complaint is that the rules different Yokai have are too vague. I'll think I've prepared dishes exactly how they want and then they'll get mad at me, so idk. 


I do not recommend this game. I was looking for a speed-based waitressing game similar to Diner Dash, which I played a ton growing up. This is not that at all. It 95% a plate-stacking mini game, but it's literally impossible. The tray doesn't move fast enough to catch all the food, and for every dish there's a million obstacles that fall that ruin everything you've caught. It's impossible to please any of the customers, fulfill their orders, or even remember what they ordered because the game just is a flurry of plates and impossible obstacles to dodge. It was so stressful and not fun at all. Did anyone even try to see if this game was playable before it was released? My poor waiter can't earn any money.

I really, really like this game, lots of fun and charm. BUT there are a few bugs that I've encountered that stop this from being a straight recommend. When things get more complex and you have unlocked all foods, several things seems to start to happen - most frustratingly, one of the yokai (Tsuchigomi) has just started being invisible in serving view! This stops me from serving her, meaning I fail her every time. This means that I can never finish the ame.

It's a very affordable game, though, and a lot of fun for my money. I do recommend it, but I do wish these bugs were fixed.

At first this game feels impossible, with too many orders, food falling too fast and a hard time balancing and fitting everything on the tray, but after getting a hang of it, it gets very entretaining! 
 
The pixelated artstyle is very charming, the gameplay is smooth and simple, the sounds are very satisfying to hear, the storyline of each yokai really makes you want to progress through the game, and even when things get pretty rushed with 40 patrons on the restaurant, I still find it relaxing to pile up all the food nicely (..◜ᴗ◝..) 
 
It may take a little while to get the flow of the game, but I'd say it's worth a try! ദ്ദി(˵ •̀ ᴗ - ˵ )

The story begins with an unpleasant supper, when your character leaves the house in anger and storms outside. This would be unremarkable on most nights, but tonight happens to be the night of the Yokai festival. Anyone who crosses the spirits’ path is instantly swept into the supernatural realm. Fortunately, you end up in a restaurant where you have to serve dishes to passing spirits in order to pay the rent demanded by your landlord, who also happens to be the chef. 
 
The gameplay is designed to be easy to understand from the very beginning. The entire experience revolves around moving between two main spaces, the restaurant floor where customers sit, and the kitchen where the food is prepared and collected. You switch between these two locations with the press of a single button. The game can be played with a gamepad, but keyboard and mouse give a steadier sense of control. 
 
At the beginning of each shift, you already know how many customers will arrive. This information is not particularly important because the number goes up with each shift. Every customer has a patience meter that steadily ticks down, so the faster you welcome them, the better. By clicking on them you can see their order, and by accepting it you send it directly to the kitchen. Serving guests on the restaurant floor is relatively easy, but the kitchen introduces the real difficulty.

The game was a delightful surprise! The art style immediately grabbed me. It perfectly captures the cozy chaos while keeping everything visually pleasing. The character and food designs are genuinely satisfying to look at (I swear I got hungry more than once).

Gameplay-wise, it’s both fun and engaging - sounds simple, but the game finds clever ways to make every tray a little adventure. There’s a rhythm to it that feels rewarding once you get into the flow, and it can be hilariously hectic in the best way.

Overall, it’s one of those games that makes you smile while testing your reflexes — a perfect mix of charm and challenge. Highly recommend!

Interesting mechanic, could've been a really amazing game if polished a little more.

I'm giving this game a thumbs up, but with an asterisk. I love the setting plus it builds off the gameplay of one of the best games of all time: 625 Sandwich Stacker. The new things like, the ability to pause orders + Gifts/Curses powerups from the yokai, is a really creative concept to keep the gameplay from getting stale. Unfortunately the Gifts/Curses is just way out of balance imo. Only a small select of yokai give actually useful Gifts, while some of their "requirements" (like stacking the meals in a highlighted area) felt too punishing and result in an automatic Curse. Then there's the soot sprites...ugh. There's gotta be a easier way to shake them off. Maybe if the devs tweak with the Gifts/Curses, I'll return to this. I'm giving this a thumbs up because there is heart here and perhaps a Hardcore Gamer(TM) will like the difficulties more than I currently am.

A stylish waiter simulator with a lot of quite interesting mechanics. Accessible training, excellent musical accompaniment and relaxed gameplay fully contribute to relaxation.
